target_moa.text: Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin, a selective relaxant binding agent that forms a 1:1 complex encapsulating rocuronium or vecuronium, thereby reversing their neuromuscular blockade.

citations.quote: Sugammadex, also known as Org25969, is a new molecular entity of the \gamma-cyclodextrin class. It was designed, by selective addition of functional groups around the structure, to bind rocuronium and vecuronium.
The drug substance (Org 25969), a modified \gamma-cyclodextrin, is an octasodium salt. The mode of action is based on the formation of 1:1 complex with rocuronium or vecuronium.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and higher than placebo): vomiting, pain, nausea, hypotension, and headache. In pooled Phase 1-3 studies at 4 mg/kg, nausea occurred in 26%, pain in 52%, and vomiting in 12%. Serious risks include anaphylaxis (0.3% of healthy volunteers) and marked bradycardia, some resulting in cardiac arrest.

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (reported in ≥10% of patients at a 2, 4, or 16 mg/kg BRIDION dose and higher than the placebo rate): vomiting, pain, nausea, hypotension, and headache. (6.1)
• Anaphylaxis: Anaphylaxis has occurred in 0.3% of healthy volunteers. Observe patients for an appropriate period of time after administration. (5.1)
• Marked Bradycardia: Cases of marked bradycardia, some of which have resulted in cardiac arrest, have been observed within minutes after administration.

basis.text: Remaining deficiencies centered on the safety profile (hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis and cardiac rhythm abnormalities) and data integrity concerns from inspections that necessitated a new confirmatory hypersensitivity study (P101).

citations.quote: However, the observations from the routine inspections indicated several protocol violations that raised questions about the integrity and reliability of the data generated from Study P101, the key study intended to address the remaining deficiency.

summary.text: BRIDION (sugammadex), a new molecular entity gamma-cyclodextrin, was submitted under section 505(b) with original receipt October 31, 2007. It underwent a protracted regulatory history — a Not Approvable letter (July 31, 2008) and a Complete Response letter (September 20, 2013) — and was presented to the AADPAC advisory committee on November 6, 2015 before being approved in December 2015 for reversal of rocuronium/vecuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade in adults undergoing surgery, with required postmarketing studies.
